newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold ends sharply higher on New York rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold ends sharply higher on New York rally.

text.p: TOCOM benchmark yen-based gold futures ended at a three-and-a-half-month high on Friday, rising in line with a strong rally overnight in New York, where speculative funds covered short positions, traders said.
They noted a growing sentiment that gold had finally formed a floor after its recent slide to three-year lows, although they predicted that further gains would be slow in coming.
TOCOM most-active December gold settled 13 yen higher at 1,377 yen per gram, the top of the session's 1,377 to 1,370 range. The other months went out 10 to 15 yen higher.
Bullion closed at $350.60/90 an ounce, little changed from New York's closing quote of $350.40/90, but up sharply from Tokyo's Thursday close at $344.70/00.

Traders said the Tokyo market was quiet despite the New York rally. Individual investors liquidated long positions on TOCOM to lock in profits, although subsequent arbitrage selling by trade houses in the bullion market was easily absorbed. Traders saw no significant selling by Australian producers.
They added that a modestly firmer yen early in the session encouraged some players to take short positions, although these were closed out in the afternoon when the yen retraced.
Despite gold's strong gains overnight, traders expected bullion prices to struggle with resistance at $354 to $355.

TOCOM December palladium ended five yen higher at 526 yen per gram, its first firmer close in a week as the contract consolidated after hitting a life-of-contract high last week of 565 yen. Players were still closely watching for new information on the long-delayed Japan-Russia 1997 supply talks and speculative fund activity in the market.
December platinum finished 10 firmer at 1,435 yen per gram, while December silver was up 2.0 yen at 207.4 yen per 10 grams.
